audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Kings / Melakhim Aleph chapter 3, first-pass draft aligned to public-domain verse structure; formal witness audit remains required.
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for dynastic marriage, high places, dream revelation, wisdom, sex-worker access to justice, infant death, maternal testimony, threatened child cutting, and fear of royal judgment.

verses.restored: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt. He took Pharaoh's daughter and brought her into City of David until he finished building his house, house of YHWH, and wall of Jerusalem around it.

familiar.text: And Solomon made affinity with Pharaoh king of Egypt, and took Pharaoh’s daughter, and brought her into the city of David, until he had made an end of building his own house, and the house of the LORD, and the wall of Jerusalem round about.

modern.text: Later, Solomon formed an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. Solomon brought her to the City of David until he had finished building his palace and the house of the LORD, as well as the wall around Jerusalem.

original.text: וַיִּתְחַתֵּ֣ן שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶת פַּרְעֹ֖ה מֶ֣לֶךְ מִצְרָ֑יִם וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת בַּת פַּרְעֹ֗ה וַיְבִיאֶ֨הָ֙ אֶל עִ֣יר דָּוִ֔ד עַ֣ד כַּלֹּת֗וֹ לִבְנ֤וֹת אֶת בֵּיתוֹ֙ וְאֶת בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וְאֶת חוֹמַ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִֽיב

verses.restored: The people were sacrificing at high places, because no house had yet been built for name of YHWH in those days.

familiar.text: Only the people sacrificed in high places, because there was no house built unto the name of the LORD, until those days.

modern.text: The people, however, were still sacrificing on the high places because a house for the Name of the LORD had not yet been built.

original.text: רַ֣ק הָעָ֔ם מְזַבְּחִ֖ים בַּבָּמ֑וֹת כִּ֠י לֹא נִבְנָ֥ה בַ֨יִת֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם יְהוָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיָּמִ֥ים הָהֵֽם

verses.restored: Solomon loved YHWH, walking in statutes of David his father; only he sacrificed and burned incense at high places.

familiar.text: And Solomon loved the LORD, walking in the statutes of David his father: only he sacrificed and burnt incense in high places.

modern.text: And Solomon loved the LORD and walked in the statutes of his father David, except that he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places.

original.text: וַיֶּאֱהַ֤ב שְׁלֹמֹה֙ אֶת יְהוָ֔ה לָלֶ֕כֶת בְּחֻקּ֖וֹת דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑יו רַ֚ק בַּבָּמ֔וֹת ה֥וּא מְזַבֵּ֖חַ וּמַקְטִֽיר

verses.restored: The king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for it was the great high place. Solomon offered one thousand burnt offerings upon that altar.

familiar.text: And the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there; for that was the great high place: a thousand burnt offerings did Solomon offer upon that altar.

modern.text: Now the king went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, for it was the great high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on the altar there.

original.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ גִּבְעֹ֨נָה֙ לִזְבֹּ֣חַ שָׁ֔ם כִּ֥י הִ֖יא הַבָּמָ֣ה הַגְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֶ֤לֶף עֹלוֹת֙ יַעֲלֶ֣ה שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה עַ֖ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֥חַ הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: At Gibeon YHWH appeared to Solomon in a dream by night. Divine said, Ask what I shall give you.

familiar.text: In Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night: and God said, Ask what I shall give thee.

modern.text: One night at Gibeon the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream, and God said, “Ask, and I will give it to you!”

original.text: בְּגִבְע֗וֹן נִרְאָ֧ה יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶל שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה בַּחֲל֣וֹם הַלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלֹהִ֔ים שְׁאַ֖ל מָ֥ה אֶתֶּן לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Solomon said, You showed great covenant-kindness to your servant David my father, as he walked before you in faithfulness, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. You kept for him this great kindness and gave him a son sitting upon his throne this day.

familiar.text: And Solomon said, Thou hast shewed unto thy servant David my father great mercy, according as he walked before thee in truth, and in righteousness, and in uprightness of heart with thee; and thou hast kept for him this great kindness, that thou hast given him a son to sit on his throne, as it is this day.

modern.text: Solomon replied, “You have shown much loving devotion to Your servant, my father David, because he walked before You in faithfulness, righteousness, and uprightness of heart. And You have maintained this loving devotion by giving him a son to sit on his throne this very day.

verses.restored: Now, YHWH my Divine, you made your servant king in place of David my father, but I am a small child; I do not know how to go out or come in.

familiar.text: And now, O LORD my God, thou hast made thy servant king instead of David my father: and I am but a little child: I know not how to go out or come in.

modern.text: And now, O LORD my God, You have made Your servant king in my father David’s place. But I am only a little child, not knowing how to go out or come in.

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔י אַתָּה֙ הִמְלַ֣כְתָּ אֶֽת עַבְדְּךָ֔ תַּ֖חַת דָּוִ֣ד אָבִ֑י וְאָֽנֹכִי֙ נַ֣עַר קָטֹ֔ן לֹ֥א אֵדַ֖ע צֵ֥את וָבֹֽא

verses.restored: Your servant is in midst of your chosen people, a great people too numerous to count.

familiar.text: And thy servant is in the midst of thy people which thou hast chosen, a great people, that cannot be numbered nor counted for multitude.

modern.text: Your servant is here among the people You have chosen, a people too numerous to count or number.

original.text: וְעַ֨בְדְּךָ֔ בְּת֥וֹךְ עַמְּךָ֖ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחָ֑רְתָּ עַם רָ֕ב אֲשֶׁ֧ר לֹֽא יִמָּנֶ֛ה וְלֹ֥א יִסָּפֵ֖ר מֵרֹֽב

verses.restored: Give your servant a listening heart to judge your people, to discern between good and evil, for who can judge this weighty people of yours?

familiar.text: Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people, that I may discern between good and bad: for who is able to judge this thy so great a people?

modern.text: Therefore give Your servant an understanding heart to judge Your people and to discern between good and evil. For who is able to govern this great people of Yours?”

original.text: וְנָתַתָּ֨ לְעַבְדְּךָ֜ לֵ֤ב שֹׁמֵ֨עַ֙ לִשְׁפֹּ֣ט אֶֽת עַמְּךָ֔ לְהָבִ֖ין בֵּֽין ט֣וֹב לְרָ֑ע כִּ֣י מִ֤י יוּכַל֙ לִשְׁפֹּ֔ט אֶת עַמְּךָ֥ הַכָּבֵ֖ד הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: The word was good in eyes of Lord, that Solomon asked this thing.

familiar.text: And the speech pleased the LORD, that Solomon had asked this thing.

modern.text: Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon had made this request.

original.text: וַיִּיטַ֥ב הַדָּבָ֖ר בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנָ֑י כִּ֚י שָׁאַ֣ל שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אֶת הַדָּבָ֖ר הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Divine said to him, Because you asked this and did not ask for long days, riches, or life of your enemies, but asked understanding to hear judgment,

familiar.text: And God said unto him, Because thou hast asked this thing, and hast not asked for thyself long life; neither hast asked riches for thyself, nor hast asked the life of thine enemies; but hast asked for thyself understanding to discern judgment;

modern.text: So God said to him, “Since you have asked for this instead of requesting long life or wealth for yourself or death for your enemies—but you have asked for discernment to administer justice—

verses.restored: look, I have done according to your word. I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so none like you was before you and none like you shall arise after you.

familiar.text: Behold, I have done according to thy words: lo, I have given thee a wise and an understanding heart; so that there was none like thee before thee, neither after thee shall any arise like unto thee.

modern.text: behold, I will do what you have asked. I will give you a wise and discerning heart, so that there has never been nor will ever be another like you.

original.text: הִנֵּ֥ה עָשִׂ֖יתִי כִּדְבָרֶ֑יךָ הִנֵּ֣ה נָתַ֣תִּי לְךָ֗ לֵ֚ב חָכָ֣ם וְנָב֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֤ר כָּמ֨וֹךָ֙ לֹא הָיָ֣ה לְפָנֶ֔יךָ וְאַחֲרֶ֖יךָ לֹא יָק֥וּם כָּמֽוֹךָ

verses.restored: I have also given what you did not ask—riches and honor—so no king shall be like you all your days.

familiar.text: And I have also given thee that which thou hast not asked, both riches, and honour: so that there shall not be any among the kings like unto thee all thy days.

modern.text: Moreover, I will give you what you did not request—both riches and honor—so that during all your days no man in any kingdom will be your equal.

original.text: וְגַ֨ם אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא שָׁאַ֨לְתָּ֙ נָתַ֣תִּי לָ֔ךְ גַּם עֹ֖שֶׁר גַּם כָּב֑וֹד אֲ֠שֶׁר לֹא הָיָ֨ה כָמ֥וֹךָ אִ֛ישׁ בַּמְּלָכִ֖ים כָּל יָמֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: If you walk in my ways, keeping my statutes and commands as David your father walked, then I will lengthen your days.

familiar.text: And if thou wilt walk in my ways, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as thy father David did walk, then I will lengthen thy days.

modern.text: So if you walk in My ways and keep My statutes and commandments, just as your father David did, I will prolong your days.”

original.text: וְאִ֣ם תֵּלֵ֣ךְ בִּדְרָכַ֗י לִשְׁמֹ֤ר חֻקַּי֙ וּמִצְוֺתַ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָלַ֖ךְ דָּוִ֣יד אָבִ֑יךָ וְהַאַרַכְתִּ֖י אֶת יָמֶֽיךָ

familiar.text: And Solomon awoke; and, behold, it was a dream. And he came to Jerusalem, and stood before the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and offered up burnt offerings, and offered peace offerings, and made a feast to all his servants.

modern.text: Then Solomon awoke, and indeed it had been a dream. So he returned to Jerusalem, stood before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings. Then he held a feast for all his servants. Solomon Judges Wisely

modern.text: At that time two prostitutes came to the king and stood before him.

modern.text: One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I live in the same house, and I gave birth while she was in the house.

familiar.text: And it came to pass the third day after that I was delivered, that this woman was delivered also: and we were together; there was no stranger with us in the house, save we two in the house.

modern.text: On the third day after I gave birth, this woman also had a baby. We were alone, with no one in the house but the two of us.

familiar.text: And this woman’s child died in the night; because she overlaid it.

modern.text: During the night this woman’s son died because she rolled over on him.

verses.restored: She arose in middle of night and took my son from beside me while your maidservant slept. She laid him in her embrace and laid her dead son in my embrace.

familiar.text: And she arose at midnight, and took my son from beside me, while thine handmaid slept, and laid it in her bosom, and laid her dead child in my bosom.

modern.text: So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my side while I was asleep. She laid him in her bosom and put her dead son at my bosom.

original.text: וַתָּקָם֩ בְּת֨וֹךְ הַלַּ֜יְלָה וַתִּקַּ֧ח אֶת בְּנִ֣י מֵֽאֶצְלִ֗י וַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ יְשֵׁנָ֔ה וַתַּשְׁכִּיבֵ֖הוּ בְּחֵיקָ֑הּ וְאֶת בְּנָ֥הּ הַמֵּ֖ת הִשְׁכִּ֥יבָה בְחֵיקִֽי

verses.restored: I arose in morning to nurse my son, and look, he was dead. But I examined him in morning, and look, it was not my son whom I bore.

familiar.text: And when I rose in the morning to give my child suck, behold, it was dead: but when I had considered it in the morning, behold, it was not my son, which I did bear.

modern.text: The next morning, when I got up to nurse my son, I discovered he was dead. But when I examined him, I realized that he was not the son I had borne.”

original.text: וָאָקֻ֥ם בַּבֹּ֛קֶר לְהֵינִ֥יק אֶת בְּנִ֖י וְהִנֵּה מֵ֑ת וָאֶתְבּוֹנֵ֤ן אֵלָיו֙ בַּבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֛ה לֹֽא הָיָ֥ה בְנִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלָֽדְתִּי

verses.restored: The other woman said, No, the living is my son and the dead is your son. The first said, No, the dead is your son and the living is my son. Thus they spoke before king.

familiar.text: And the other woman said, Nay; but the living is my son, and the dead is thy son. And this said, No; but the dead is thy son, and the living is my son. Thus they spake before the king.

modern.text: “No,” said the other woman, “the living one is my son and the dead one is your son.” But the first woman insisted, “No, the dead one is yours and the living one is mine.” So they argued before the king.

verses.restored: The king said, This one says, This is my living son and your son is dead; and that one says, No, your son is dead and my son is living.

familiar.text: Then said the king, The one saith, This is my son that liveth, and thy son is the dead: and the other saith, Nay; but thy son is the dead, and my son is the living.

modern.text: Then the king replied, “This woman says, ‘My son is alive and yours is dead,’ but that woman says, ‘No, your son is dead and mine is alive.’”

verses.restored: The king said, Bring me a sword. They brought sword before king.

familiar.text: And the king said, Bring me a sword. And they brought a sword before the king.

modern.text: The king continued, “Bring me a sword.” So they brought him a sword,

familiar.text: And the king said, Divide the living child in two, and give half to the one, and half to the other.

modern.text: and the king declared, “Cut the living child in two and give half to one and half to the other.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ גִּזְר֛וּ אֶת הַיֶּ֥לֶד הַחַ֖י לִשְׁנָ֑יִם וּתְנ֤וּ אֶֽת הַחֲצִי֙ לְאַחַ֔ת וְאֶֽת הַחֲצִ֖י לְאֶחָֽת

verses.restored: The woman whose son was living spoke to king, for her womb/compassion burned for her son: Please, my lord, give her living child, and killing do not kill him. But the other said, Neither mine nor yours—divide him.

familiar.text: Then spake the woman whose the living child was unto the king, for her bowels yearned upon her son, and she said, O my lord, give her the living child, and in no wise slay it. But the other said, Let it be neither mine nor thine, but divide it.

modern.text: Then the woman whose son was alive spoke to the king because she yearned with compassion for her son. “Please, my lord,” she said, “give her the living baby. Do not kill him!” But the other woman said, “He will be neither mine nor yours. Cut him in two!”

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר הָאִשָּׁה֩ אֲשֶׁר בְּנָ֨הּ הַחַ֜י אֶל הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ כִּֽי נִכְמְר֣וּ רַחֲמֶיהָ֮ עַל בְּנָהּ֒ וַתֹּ֣אמֶר בִּ֣י אֲדֹנִ֗י תְּנוּ לָהּ֙ אֶת הַיָּל֣וּד הַחַ֔י וְהָמֵ֖ת אַל תְּמִיתֻ֑הוּ וְזֹ֣את אֹמֶ֗רֶת גַּם לִ֥י גַם לָ֛ךְ לֹ֥א יִהְיֶ֖ה גְּזֹֽרוּ

verses.restored: The king answered, Give her living child, and killing do not kill him; she is his mother.

familiar.text: Then the king answered and said, Give her the living child, and in no wise slay it: she is the mother thereof.

modern.text: Then the king gave his ruling: “Give the living baby to the first woman. By no means should you kill him; she is his mother.”

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר תְּנוּ לָהּ֙ אֶת הַיָּל֣וּד הַחַ֔י וְהָמֵ֖ת לֹ֣א תְמִיתֻ֑הוּ הִ֖יא אִמּֽוֹ

verses.restored: All Israel heard judgment king judged, and they feared king, for they saw wisdom of Divine was within him to do justice.

familiar.text: And all Israel heard of the judgment which the king had judged; and they feared the king: for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him, to do judgment.

modern.text: When all Israel heard of the judgment the king had given, they stood in awe of him, for they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמְע֣וּ כָל יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֶת הַמִּשְׁפָּט֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁפַ֣ט הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיִּֽרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י רָא֔וּ כִּֽי חָכְמַ֧ת אֱלֹהִ֛ים בְּקִרְבּ֖וֹ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת מִשְׁפָּֽט

translation_notes: Pharaoh's daughter enters the story as a diplomatic marriage partner whose consent, name, and political experience are not recorded. International alliance does not make a woman transferable property.
Solomon asks for a listening heart. Wisdom is accountable discernment for people, not brilliance, wealth, certainty, or domination.
The two women are identified by stigmatized labor yet receive direct access to the king. Their occupation does not reduce credibility, motherhood, grief, or legal standing.
The dead infant's death is narrated through accidental overlaying in ancient sleeping conditions. It must not be used to shame bereaved parents or claim certainty about modern infant deaths.
The sword threat is a dangerous judicial performance involving a living child. It should not be copied as interrogation, custody practice, or proof that threats reveal truth.
The compassionate response helps Solomon identify the mother in the narrative, but maternal worth cannot be reduced to self-erasure or willingness to surrender a child.
Israel fears the king after the judgment. Admiration and fear are not identical to safe, transparent, appealable justice.
safety_note: Do not use Solomon's test as a model for threatening children, coercive custody decisions, or traumatizing witnesses. Do not stigmatize sex workers or bereaved parents. A listening heart must center safety, evidence, access, and the least harmful path.
